question: what do the fit and the vignette stresses become without the records whose older-years column, exchange line or development-table history the filing readings could not settle?
source: data/aggregated_column_review.json (confidence low_confidence), data/fx_untranslated_excluded.json (reason undeterminable_kept) and data/restated_base_excluded.json (history_restated); the readings are archived in results/extraction_error_rate/mature-cohort/round2/ and round5/
operator_construction: size-only operator: gamma fixed at 0 in the likelihood (the headline fit); a refit, not a zeroing: k, sigma_undiv, sigma_div, nu_clean and nu_RITC are that fit's own posterior. sigma does not depend on H, so the concentration channel of any decomposition is exactly zero
rule: without the 39 records the filing readings could not settle: 6 older-years columns marked low_confidence in data/aggregated_column_review.json, 4 exchange lines marked undeterminable_kept in data/fx_untranslated_excluded.json and 29 tables whose history restated, listed under history_restated in data/restated_base_excluded.json

left_out.why: older-years column, construction could not be settled (calendar_year): X1 and Y2 calendar_year, from the shape of the year t table alone (no year t-1 table in the corpus: the column is a flat stock re-estimated at successive year ends, and the 2016 report's 'Provision in respect of prior years' covers the same pre-2011 set). The adopted -118.31 (column in) stands; with the column out the figure would be -86.114. The evidence is structural only, so the record is low confidence.

development table's history restated, kept under rule 6 (unexplained_history_move): UY2014's end-2020 cell in the 2021 table (187,147) is 10.3m above the 2020 report's printed estimate and out of line with its own column (169,537 -> 187,147 -> 170,900), unexplained in the filing (P1, Q8): 2.1% of R (498.1m). The rest moves by the stated retranslation; the table ties to the balance sheet and its incurred gap (-8.7%) is the 2020 control's (-6.9%), the pre-2011 years outside the table. M as printed (+20.409m) stands. Rule 1 under the exact control clause (23 October 2026, review 8): not met. The control miss is -6.9% (over 5%, within 10%, the same pre-2011 years outside the table in both years), but the year t miss, -8.7%, is 1.3 times the control's, not three times, and is itself under 10%. The record stays least certain

development table's history restated, kept under rule 6 (take_on_base_bounded): rule 5b (U1, U2). An external RITC 'in the year' of reserves relating only to the 2020 and 2021 underwriting years (p47); counterparty, date and amount are not printed, and note 4's gross roll-forward (p31) has no transfer row (2,050,580 + 733,886 - 79,491 - 544,404 - 10,867 = 2,149,704, USD 000). The only ADC is outward, bought in 2020 (p49), so not a take-on. R is the opening USD 2,050.580m (p31), which is the analysis's opening (GBP 1,637.71m) and includes no acquired reserves. The filing bounds the take-on: the 2024 table's 2020 and 2021 columns exceed the 2023 filing's at every age while the control columns move about -1%, and the acquired cumulative incurred at the latest comparable ages is 105.138m + 58.940m = USD 164.078m (U1, U2); the reserves taken on are that incurred less the acquired paid to date, so they cannot exceed it: at most 8.0% of R (U2 puts it at about 2 to 3% on a low-confidence indicative range). The table carries the acquired years as if always, so the movement within the table (-33.258m USD = -26.56m GBP, u <= 2022, equal to the analysis figure) excludes the take-on and only the divisor is short; the acquired years' own pre-acquisition development (-22.091m of it) is in the figure. Bounded at or below 10% of R: the record stays and joins the least-certain list

Share of R, checked after review 8 against rule 6's 1% of R (opening gross claims outstanding 1,601.0m, note 9(a), so 16.01m): the 2016 table's end-2015 cells are 761.5 (UY2013) and 804.7 (UY2014) against 786.4 and 821.4 in the 2015 report, falls of 24.9m (1.56% of R) and 16.7m (1.04% of R), 41.6m together (2.60%), both cells that the exchange uplift (ratios 1.016, 1.074, 0.968, 0.980 for UY2011-UY2014, no common factor) should have raised, so the move beyond the exchange rate is at least the fall; P6's own measure, about 2% of the year's gross incurred (1,089.5m), is 21.8m or 1.4% of R. development table's history restated, kept under rule 6 (take_on_table_unreconciled): added after review 8 (decision of the Claude analysis session, 23 October 2026), on the same all-prior-years scope as 3500/2023. RITCs of Syndicates 1897, 2468 and 1980/2014/2001 effective 1 January 2022 and loss portfolio transfers (p4; note 7 p30 'Reinsurance of new liabilities 1,728,476'), the history carried as if always (the 2018 column about double the 2021 report's, Q7). The RITCs are in R (3,955.045m USD = 2,615.345 + 1,339.7, data/opening_reserves_takeon_base.json), so rule 5 changes nothing. But the table does not reconcile with note 7's change in estimates including foreign exchange of -293.1m (-293,072, p30) on that scope: the movement on every column that existed at end-2021 (2013-2019 and 2021) is -291.756m - 98.057m = -389.8m (review 8; P6's workings), and the whole table (those columns plus the new 2022 column, +363.424m) is -26.4m, a gap of 266.7m (P6; Q7 -26.389m); only the 2013-2019 columns alone (-291.8m, the adopted figure) are within 0.4% of it. Either way the acquired share outside R is at most 9.1% of R for the two mid-2022 LPTs (360.9m of 3,955.045m) and 9.8% with all four (388.7m), at or below rule 5b's 10%, so rule 5b would list the record too.
